criteria.name: Communication

descriptors.0: Nothing reached the channel while the incident was open, or only after the lead had to chase you repeatedly.
descriptors.1: You posted, but late or without saying what was wrong; the lead had to ask and nudge.
descriptors.2: Some timely updates, but at least one gap or one post that did not say what you had found.
descriptors.3: Prompt, useful updates with one slip: a late answer to the lead, or a quiet stretch.
descriptors.4: A first update in the first two minutes, the lead's request answered at once, no quiet stretch, and the cause named in plain words.

criteria.keep: Keep posting a short status as soon as you know something, even when it is only 'still looking'.

rules.plain: Post a first update in #incident-duplicates within 2 minutes of the start.
rules.label: a first update inside two minutes
rules.advice: Post a first update in the channel within two minutes, even if it is only what you have seen so far.

rules.plain: When Aarav asks for an update, answer within a minute.
rules.label: the lead's request answered at once
rules.advice: When the lead asks for an update, answer within a minute, even if nothing has changed.

rules.plain: Never let 5 quiet minutes pass without a post, so Aarav does not have to nudge you.
rules.label: no quiet stretch of five minutes
rules.advice: Set a timer for each promised update: do not let five quiet minutes pass without a post.

rules.plain: Say in the channel what you found: that the database has no unique constraint or index for a slot (migration 0006 only made a plain, non-unique index).
rules.label: the cause named in the channel
rules.advice: Say what you found, not only that you are working on it: the database has no unique constraint or index for a slot, so a second booking is accepted. The duplicate rows alone are a symptom.

criteria.name: Diagnosis

descriptors.0: You changed things before you had run the tests or opened anything that explains the double bookings.
descriptors.1: You saw that the tests failed but never looked at the data or at what the database enforces.
descriptors.2: You looked at the right places, but after you had already started editing, or only with a pointer.
descriptors.3: Reproduce, look at the data, find the missing constraint: three of the four habits, in order.
descriptors.4: You reproduced it, read the production data and the migration that made the index before your first edit, and needed no pointer.

criteria.keep: Keep reproducing first and reading the real data and the schema before you write a migration.

rules.plain: Run the tests before you save any file, and read why they fail.
rules.label: the tests run before the first edit
rules.advice: Run the tests and read the first error line of each failure before you change anything.

rules.plain: Open the production snapshot (fixtures/prod_snapshot.sql), or search the project for the duplicates, before your first save.
rules.label: the production data looked at before editing
rules.advice: Look at the real rows before you write a migration: a change that is right on an empty table can fail on production data.

rules.plain: Open the migration that created the index on appointments (0006 or 0002), or search for UNIQUE, before your first save.
rules.label: the missing constraint found before editing
rules.advice: The second booking succeeded because nothing refused it: read the migration that made the index and ask what it enforces.

rules.plain: Find the missing constraint yourself, before Rohan has to point at it (about 4 minutes in).
rules.label: found without a pointer
rules.advice: Look at what the database enforces yourself before you wait for a teammate to point at it.

criteria.name: Fix quality

descriptors.0: The migration is missing, or it fails on the production data, or the suite is still red on main.
descriptors.1: Only one part of the problem is solved: the index, or the clean-up, but not both.
descriptors.2: Two of the four: for example rows resolved and a green suite but no index, or an index that blocks cancelled slots.
descriptors.3: A correct migration with one thing to improve: a missing reason, or an earliest booking that was not kept.
descriptors.4: No row deleted, the duplicates resolved the way the incident asks, a partial unique index on Booked rows, and the whole suite green on my re-run.

criteria.keep: Keep running a migration against a copy of the real data before you ship it, and keep every record.

rules.plain: Delete no appointment: every row of the production snapshot is still there after your migration. The debrief upgrades the snapshot with it.
rules.label: no appointment deleted
rules.advice: Cancel the later duplicates instead of deleting them: a patient's record is not yours to remove.

rules.plain: Keep the earliest booking of each double-booked slot, set the later ones to Cancelled and record why (a new column or a log table).
rules.label: the double bookings resolved, with the reason recorded
rules.advice: Keep the earliest booking of each slot, cancel the later ones and record why in a new column or a log table.

rules.plain: Add a unique index on doctor, date and time that applies only to Booked rows, so cancelled and completed rows can share a slot.
rules.label: a partial unique index on the Booked rows
rules.advice: Add CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... (doctor_id, date, slot_at) WHERE status = 'Booked': it must exist after the clean-up, and only for Booked rows.

rules.plain: The whole test suite passes on the merged project. The debrief re-runs it.
rules.label: the whole suite green on my re-run
rules.advice: Run the whole suite, not only the acceptance tests, before you submit.

criteria.name: Testing

descriptors.0: You submitted without ever running the tests, and nothing protects the fix.
descriptors.1: You ran the tests, but not green before submitting, and nothing protects the fix.
descriptors.2: A green run before submit and no red submit, but no new test that proves the fix.
descriptors.3: Green before submit, no red submit, and a regression test that was added but does not prove the fix.
descriptors.4: A green run before submit, no red submit, and a regression test that books a slot twice, fails on the old code and passes on yours.

criteria.keep: Keep adding a regression test with every bug fix: it is the part that outlives the incident.

rules.plain: Run the tests after your last change and see them green before you press Submit.
rules.label: a green run of your own before Submit
rules.advice: Run the tests yourself and see them green before you press Submit.

rules.plain: Do not submit while tests still fail: a submit that is refused for failing tests counts against you.
rules.label: no red submit
rules.advice: Submit only when your own run is green: a red submit costs a round trip.

rules.plain: Add a regression test in tests/regression/ (test_regression_<what>.py).
rules.label: a regression test added
rules.advice: Add a regression test in tests/regression/ for the bug you fixed.

rules.plain: Your regression test books the same slot twice, fails on the old code and passes on your fix. The debrief runs it both ways.
rules.label: a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after
rules.advice: Book the same slot twice and expect 409: run your new test before the migration, it has to be red then, and green after.

criteria.name: Ownership

descriptors.0: The fix was not accepted, or it came long after the clinic opened with no word to the team.
descriptors.1: Accepted late, with many hints and no word to the team.
descriptors.2: Accepted, but you leaned on hints or went outside your files.
descriptors.3: Accepted in time, you stayed inside your files and asked for little help, but you did not close the loop.
descriptors.4: Accepted inside the time box, inside your own files, with one hint at most, and the team told that the fix was ready.

criteria.keep: Keep telling the team when the fix is ready and what you did.

rules.plain: Get the fix accepted inside the 30 minutes.
rules.label: accepted inside the time box
rules.advice: Watch the clock: the clinic opens at 09:00, so aim to have the fix submitted inside the time box.

rules.plain: Use at most one hint. Every answer to a question of yours counts, and so does a pointer you needed.
rules.label: at most one hint
rules.advice: Try the next step on your own before you ask a teammate; every answer counts as a hint.

rules.plain: Only change files your role may edit (database/ and tests/regression/): backend/ is Rohan's, so Submit is refused if you touch it.
rules.label: inside your own files
rules.advice: Read the list of files you may edit in the task document before you change anything outside it: the booking route is Rohan's.

rules.plain: After your last green run, tell the channel the fix is ready.
rules.label: the team told that the fix was ready
rules.advice: When the tests are green, tell the channel the fix is ready and what you changed.
